title: VaultTec — Phase 4d Fresh-Window Test Report
method: Fresh-window test of the Phase 4c winners only: wide-5 (5% stop / 7.5% target) and wide-6 (6% / 9%), for RSI and Bollinger mean-reversion, plus the baseline (3% / 4.5%) as a control, on three fresh 180-calendar-day windows never used for selection (FRESH-1/2/3, all ending before OOS-3 starts). Delayed real market history from yfinance (free), 70 days of warm-up history before each window, 12 symbols, 5-day walk-forward steps, signals from history up to the trade day only — no look-ahead. Every trade goes through the real PaperTradingEngine and Risk Engine, balanced profile, $10,000 virtual cash, long-only, 10-day exit. Every variant keeps a stop-loss; the stop is never removed. Fetched histories are cached to data/fresh-cache/ as they arrive, so an interrupted run resumes from disk instead of re-fetching. Fresh results are pooled ONLY across the fresh windows — never with the selection windows, which are not re-run here.
data_source: yfinance (delayed real market data, free — Yahoo Finance)
verdict_rule: A variant 'holds up' on fresh data when its pooled fresh-window paper P&L is > $0 AND its pooled win rate is > 40% (the 1.5:1 break-even) AND it is positive in at least 2 of the 3 fresh windows.

bollinger.verdict_rule: holds up = pooled fresh P&L > $0 AND pooled win rate > 40% AND positive in at least 2 of 3 fresh windows

note: Fresh-window results are the honest check on Phase 4c: the wide-stop variants were picked because they looked good on OOS-1/2/3, so those windows cannot confirm them. A variant that holds up here — positive pooled, above break-even win rate, positive in at least 2 of 3 fresh windows — has survived a genuinely new test; a variant that fades or reverses here means the Phase 4c result was selection luck, and the wider stop should not be trusted on its own. Nothing here proves future profits: past performance does not guarantee future results, and live paper trades over real days plus a compliance/legal review are still required before any real money is considered.
